assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new class of tunable flat-band quantum matter (correlated insulators, superconductivity) with a clear, original, experimentally decisive discovery and a theory that predicted the magic angle. As an experimentalist in materials physics I value that the effect is controlled by a geometric parameter in an engineered interface.
assessment.attribution: The flat-band prediction (Bistritzer and MacDonald) and the 2018 experimental discovery (Jarillo-Herrero group) form a natural theory-plus-experiment pairing. Early-career experimental co-authors are not in the credited list, so the group credit cannot be fully reflected; the three names are the best supported fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many independent groups across twisted multilayers and moire systems within a few years; the interpretation of the correlated phases is still evolving, but the core discovery is robust. Timing is reasonable though arguably early.
uncertainties: Whether the superconductivity mechanism is settled is unclear to me.
Contributions of other theorists and of first-author experimentalists may be disputed or omitted from the credited names.
I have not independently verified priority details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction in electron optics overcame a limit (spherical aberration) that had held since Scherzer, delivering sub-angstrom TEM and STEM imaging and spectroscopy now routine in materials physics. It is a genuine invention with lasting enabling impact, which fits the 'discovery or invention' criterion.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theory and designs of correctors, Haider led the TEM corrector realization and Krivanek the STEM corrector and its use for atomic-resolution spectroscopy. Other key contributors (notably Knut Urban for the TEM program, and Batson et al.) are outside the credited list, so credit is not complete.
assessment.maturity: Instruments are widely deployed and independently confirmed worldwide; recognition is mature and arguably overdue. Because this is my own field, I disclose a possible bias and have tried to rank it below the discoveries I judge decisively original in physics.
uncertainties: Allocation among Rose, Haider, Krivanek and Urban is genuinely contested.
Whether the committee views this as physics rather than instrumentation/chemistry-adjacent method.
Possible subjective bias from my own TEM background.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised the Hubbard model and enabled quantum simulation of correlated matter, including the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, Fermi-Hubbard physics and quantum gas microscopy. Broad, deep impact across condensed matter, AMO and quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Greiner and Bloch with Hansch demonstrated the Mott transition; Bloch and Esslinger developed fermionic and lattice platforms; Cirac and Zoller proposed the theoretical basis (Zoller with Jaksch). Choosing experimentalists is defensible but leaves theory credit to be argued, and BEC itself was already recognized in 2001.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with many independent labs and a continually growing field; recognition would be timely or somewhat late.
uncertainties: Experiment versus theory allocation (Zoller and Cirac versus Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger).
Overlap with the 2001 BEC prize area.
Exact priority of key experiments recalled from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks with the magic-wavelength concept reached 10^-18 fractional uncertainty, enabling tests of relativity and fundamental constants at the redshift level of centimetres and opening a route to redefining the second. Clear, quantitative, lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and demonstrated the magic-wavelength lattice clock concept; Ye drove the record accuracy and spectroscopy of many-body lattice clocks. Two natural names, though Hall/Hansch combs (already recognised in 2005) and ion-clock work lie outside this candidate.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by several national labs and groups; the redefinition of the second is still pending, so the practical culmination is not yet completed, but the discovery/invention itself is mature.
uncertainties: Whether ion clocks (Wineland-related, already recognised) and other groups share needed credit.
Timing relative to redefinition of the second.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum anomalous Hall effect gives quantized Hall conductance without an external magnetic field, a clean realisation of topological transport in magnetic topological insulators, with materials-physics growth challenges overcome by molecular-beam epitaxy. Important and original, and conceptually clear.
assessment.attribution: Fang and Dai with collaborators made the theoretical proposal for magnetically doped topological insulators; Xue's group made the 2013 experimental observation. Haldane's earlier model (recognised in 2016) and other contributors (e.g. Chang, Zhang) complicate the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Observed first at very low temperatures, since reproduced by other groups with improved samples; interpretation stable, applications (metrology) still developing. Moderately mature.
uncertainties: Credit among theory proposals and the 2013 experiment may be disputed.
Overlap with the 2016 topological-phase prize.
Operating temperature and device maturity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson confirmed the mechanism recognised in 2013 and is one of the major discoveries of the century, involving decades of detector and analysis innovation.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across two giant collaborations; the candidate lists four names and the statutes allow at most three. Any selection of spokespersons or conceivers involves arbitrary judgement; I choose among the credited names but this is the weakest part of the case.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by two experiments and extended by subsequent measurements; recognition is timely, with the main obstacle being attribution rather than science.
uncertainties: Collaboration scale makes a fair three-person allocation very difficult.
I cannot verify the exact roles of each named individual.
Choice versus the LHC-construction candidate is judgement-based.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser is a bandgap-engineered intersubband laser, a true invention that created compact mid-infrared and terahertz sources with broad use in spectroscopy and sensing. Strong 'invention' case with strong materials-physics (epitaxy) content.
assessment.attribution: Capasso led the 1994 demonstration at Bell Labs, Faist as first author and key developer, and Cho supplied molecular-beam epitaxy growth. The earlier Kazarinov-Suris proposal is not in the credited list, which complicates the priority picture.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and commercialised over three decades; mature and, if anything, long established.
uncertainties: Priority relationship with the 1971 theoretical proposal.
Whether the committee sees the growth contribution as co-decisive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED achieved strong coupling between single microwave photons and superconducting artificial atoms, the architecture behind much of present superconducting quantum information and a clean platform for quantum optics on a chip.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin and Schoelkopf with Wallraff and others proposed and demonstrated the architecture (2004); the credited trio is plausible but experimental co-leads (e.g. Wallraff) are not credited. I recall the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits, which is related but distinct, and I cannot verify how the committee would see the overlap.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced and heavily built upon by many groups; science is mature, but near-term recognition might be seen as redundant with recent superconducting-circuit recognition.
uncertainties: Overlap with a recent related prize.
Missing experimental co-originator in credited names.
Whether the discovery is separable from the engineering of quantum computers.
